articles.title: Fat people cannot win, regardless of what we do. And I’ve had enough
articles.summary: Using weight loss drugs like Ozempic is not ‘cheating’ – and why does it matter how a person changes their body anyway? As you might know if you read my columns, see me a mile away, or talk to me for five seconds, I am a card-carrying lifelong member of the Fat Lesbian Club.
body: It’s not Goodman’s 74-year-old body (his choice) I want to discuss, but instead the arguments that broke out about how he lost the weight. On one side there were many people congratulating him on his hard work. Then there were people claiming he had taken Ozempic so it wasn’t actually hard work, and then there were people defending that by saying he’d been losing weight for years, so he’d done it the “right way”, actually.

I don’t know the details and I don’t care, but none of this is good. This is a common sentiment, but now it seems to be snowballing. There’s this idea that fat people who use weight loss drugs are “cheating” or “taking the easy way”. What it means, as usual, is that fat people cannot win, regardless of what we do. And I’ve had enough.

articles.title: Where did all the XXL clothes go? Fashion brands are scrapping plus sizes in the GLP-1 era
articles.summary: As weight-loss drugs gain popularity in the US, brands are scaling back their ranges – and frustrating customers. In March 2023, the model, activist and writer Tess Holliday announced that she had been working as a size and inclusivity consultant for H&M.
body: This bucked a trend, coming at an otherwise gloomy time for plus-sized fashion. By 2023, the fashion industry was in the grips of an Ozempic-fuelled celebration of skinny bodies, after its brief flirtation with curves during the body positivity movement of the late 2010s.

But by 2026, just three years after the H&M partnership was announced, the fruits of the project had vanished. The research firm Edited, which tracks items as they launch on retailers’ websites, analysed H&M’s offerings for spring/summer 2026, recording all new women’s dresses landing on the site from January to May and compared it with the same period in 2025. Last year, 3XL and 4XL made up 2% of the new inventory. This year those sizes were entirely absent. Other large sizes fell too: XXL, which had accounted for 13.3% of inventory in 2025, was down 3 percentage points, while XL was down 2 percentage points, and smaller sizes, XS to large, rose by 3 percentage points on average.
points: As weight-loss drugs gain popularity in the US, brands are scaling back their ranges – and frustrating customers.

articles.title: JD Sports cuts £50m from profit forecast as cost of living pressures hit trainer sales
articles.summary: Inflation fuelled by Iran conflict deterring shoppers, especially in the US, says high street chain. The sports fashion retailer JD has cut £50m from its profit forecast as cost of living pressures, fuelled by the US war on Iran, weighed on sales of trainers.
body: JD Sports, which sells brands including Nike and Adidas, said widespread inflation had hit shoppers’ wallets, particularly its core young shoppers, resulting in a drop in sales across important markets such as the US, where it struggled to shift trainers and other footwear.

Bosses went on to warn that the wider fall in consumer spending was likely to continue into the second half of the year. The retailer now expects lower pre-tax profits of between £700m and £800m for the full year, having previously hoped to reach £750m to £850m.
The news led to a 14% drop in JD’s London-listed shares by Thursday afternoon trading, to their lowest level since May.

Régis Schultz, JD’s chief executive, said: “Trading in the second quarter remained tough,” adding that the company had been forced to cut prices and offer promotions to compensate, as “our core consumer was impacted by incremental cost-of-living pressures.”

articles.title: This Rural Village in Spain is Welcoming Digital Nomads With Open Arms
articles.summary: As Spain's major cities struggle with overtourism, 8,000 rural villages are at risk of total depopulation. Can remote workers help bridge the gap?
body: Rooral was featured on Condé Nast Traveler' s Bright Ideas in Travel 2025. Read the full list of winners here.

In Spain, headlines and images of abandoned towns warn of rapid depopulation in the country’s smallest villages. Many fear that Spain’s vibrant culture will be left behind as rural populations thin out. But when I recently spent a month in Benarraba, a picturesque Andalusian village tucked into the mountains with just 350 permanent residents, those concerns seemed far away.

Strolling along the winding cobblestone streets lined with quaint white-washed buildings, I would pass a group of teenagers on their way to a coding workshop followed by a dozen women well into retirement age walking to the padel court with a 30-year-old traveler from South Korea. By sunset, I would take my spot in the community kitchen to make pasta topped with parsley from my neighbor’s garden and run next door to borrow chairs. Soon, the dinner table would be filled by people from all around the world.

articles.title: 29 Vintage Photos of a Young Martha Stewart Before She Was a Lifestyle Icon
articles.summary: Vogue revisits the culinary queen, tastemaker, and lifestyle super-influencer Martha Stewart in her pre-fame days as a rising model and aspiring businesswoman.
body: Before her name became a byword for “good taste,” Martha Stewart was born Martha Kostyra, the oldest daughter of six children in a well-to-do Polish Catholic family. Raised in Nutley, New Jersey, she displayed an entrepreneurial knack from an early age: A 10-year-old Martha booked her first paid gig by planning birthday parties for the kids in her neighborhood. She began modeling as a teenager, earning $50 an hour to appear in ad campaigns for the likes of Chanel and Tareyton cigarettes. With her 5’9” frame and knockout beauty, Stewart’s modeling portfolio radiates the same mix of cold charm and playful sensuality that would later define her entire brand.

Raised by parents who passed on their love of cooking and gardening, Stewart left Wall Street in the mid-’70s to start a catering company out of the basement of Turkey Hill, her iconic former residence in Westport, Connecticut. Her kitchen skills and elegant aesthetic earned her a reputation among any East Coaster lucky enough to attend one of her famed garden parties.
points: Vogue revisits the culinary queen, tastemaker, and lifestyle super-influencer Martha Stewart in her pre-fame days as a rising model and aspiring businesswoman.

articles.title: Giant Garlic Knot
articles.summary: This savory babka is braided with a whole head of garlic, fresh parsley, and salty Parmesan.
body: In this fun mashup, billowy garlic knots from your favorite slice shop meet braided babka, a Jewish delicacy. The dough, enriched with eggs, butter, and sugar, is gloriously fluffy, wrapped around the rich filling. Made with both fresh garlic and garlic powder, plus Parmesan, butter, and fresh parsley, the filling goes all in on the savory funk. Once out of the oven, the XL knot is brushed with a garlic-infused olive oil, plus more cheese for good measure to really bring home the garlic knot vibes. Another must? A sidecar of marinara.
The dough is kneaded entirely by hand but a stand mixer will make quick work of a batch. It will start out very sticky at the beginning; add flour judiciously to help things along.

articles.title: Coty Sales Fall 1% as It Gears Up for “Transition Year”
articles.summary: Coty ended 2026 on a high note, with Q4 results beating analyst expectations. Now, it’s preparing for the next phase of growth.
body: Coty said on Thursday that like-for-like revenues were down 1% to $1.3 billion in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, falling 5% to $5.8 billion for the full year. Shares dipped 7% in after-hours trading due to the company withholding its 2027 outlook.

“We closed 2026 on a stronger note, delivering sales and profit ahead of our targets, and growing free cash flow even in the face of business headwinds, all while establishing a clear strategic framework and taking decisive action to strengthen our core business in 2027 and beyond,” Markus Strobel, executive chair and interim CEO, said in a statement. The executive said that the Coty.Curated strategic framework has now entered execution, with the rightsizing of Coty’s commercial organization, consumer beauty R&D, and global brand marketing functions underway.

Strobel said that the company is encouraged to see closer alignment between its sell-in and sell-out numbers. That said, he noted that Coty remains uncontent with its sell-out performance, which remains below market levels in both prestige and consumer beauty divisions, and that closing the gap is a priority across the organization.
points: Coty ended 2026 on a high note, with Q4 results beating analyst expectations.
Now, it’s preparing for the next phase of growth.

articles.title: The 9 Major Benefits of Walking After Dinner
articles.summary: Walking after eating is proven to benefit our overall health. Here, Heather Viola, DO, primary-care physician at Mount Sinai Doctors-Ansonia breaks down all the reasons why and how to incorporate it into your daily routine.
body: After a big meal at night, even the lightest form of physical activity may be the furthest thing from your mind. But as it turns out, walking after eating has many benefits.

We’re not just talking about boosting our endorphins or reducing stress levels when taking a leisurely, serotonin-inducing strolls. Walking after eating has been proven to do many things for our overall health, and it’s definitely something to consider for future meals. But don’t just take our word for it. Below, Heather Viola, DO, primary-care physician at Mount Sinai Doctors-Ansonia, breaks down all the reasons you should be taking a post-meal walk after breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

Both times can be beneficial, just in different ways. Dr. Viola explains that walking before your body has ingested food will enact different chemical reactions than walking after eating. Walking before a meal helps burn stored fat efficiently and assists with weight loss. When you walk half an hour or so after eating, she says, it can decrease the amount of sugar and fats that accumulate in your bloodstream. It can also give your body more energy to exercise, digest, and regulate blood sugar levels more effectively.
points: Walking after eating is proven to benefit our overall health.
